split_reasoning: Three activities: handling cash and banking, bookkeeping entries, and bank transactions; cash handling is often live at a counter but for a general clerk it is mostly back-office cash and deposit work, so split cash/banking from bookkeeping.

parts.text: Collect, count and disburse money and complete bank transactions such as deposits.
parts.type_reasoning: Each cash count and deposit ends in a reconciled amount and bank slip that others rely on, done in the office rather than with a customer waiting.
parts.unit_reasoning: Cash is counted and deposited or paid out as one batch, which is handed to the bank or the finance owner.
parts.work_item: one cash count and deposit or disbursement
parts.start: cash, checks or payment requests gathered
parts.end: amounts counted, deposit made or payment handed out, and record of the total kept
parts.checked_by: office manager or bookkeeper; the bank

parts.text: Do basic bookkeeping entries for the office's transactions.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces ledger entries that the manager or accountant relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Entries are posted in a batch from the day's or week's transactions and reviewed at period end.
parts.work_item: one batch of bookkeeping entries (e.g. a day's or week's transactions posted)
parts.end: entries posted to the books

notes: Time shares are a guess; some small offices collect payment at a counter, which would be LIVE_SERVICE.

split_reasoning: Joins live conversations with customers and staff (answering, taking orders, complaints) and explaining information to employees; the main division is live contacts versus written replies.

parts.text: Talk with a customer or employee in person or by phone to answer a question, take an order, or handle a complaint.
parts.type_reasoning: The person is waiting while the question is answered or the order is taken.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each contact is resolved within one conversation.
parts.work_item: one customer or employee enquiry, order or complaint handled in a live contact
parts.start: person asks a question or raises an issue
parts.end: answer given, order taken or complaint logged and person satisfied or referred
parts.checked_by: the customer or employee; office manager for complaints

parts.text: Send written explanations or information to employees or customers.
parts.type_reasoning: Written messages are sent later and relied on by recipients.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each message or notice is sent as a whole to its recipients.
parts.work_item: one written reply or information notice sent
parts.start: question or need for information arises
parts.end: message sent

notes: Very generic statement; heavy overlap with phone answering and correspondence statements.

split_reasoning: One activity: handling incoming calls by answering, routing and recording messages.

parts.text: Answer an incoming call, direct it to the right person, or take a message.
parts.type_reasoning: The caller is on the line throughout, and the call is handled in the conversation.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each call is answered and resolved or passed on within one contact.
parts.work_item: one incoming call answered, transferred or message taken
parts.start: phone rings and clerk picks up
parts.end: call transferred or message written and caller ends the call
parts.checked_by: the caller and the person receiving the call or message

split_reasoning: Compiling, copying and sorting records is one back-office routine whose product is filed records.

parts.text: Compile, copy, sort and file records of office activities and transactions.
parts.type_reasoning: Produces organized filed records others later retrieve.
parts.unit_reasoning: Records are handled in batches as they accumulate and filed away as a set.
parts.work_item: one batch of records compiled, copied and filed
parts.start: batch of documents or transaction records collected
parts.end: records sorted and placed in the filing system

split_reasoning: One activity: completing and mailing outgoing financial and legal documents; the documents are alike in being prepared and sent.

parts.text: Complete and mail bills, contracts, policies, invoices or checks.
parts.type_reasoning: Each batch yields documents sent to customers or vendors that they rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Documents are prepared and mailed in a billing run or batch.
parts.work_item: one batch of bills, invoices, contracts or checks prepared and mailed
parts.end: documents completed and mailed

split_reasoning: Operating machines is a means to other deliverables (copies, scans, faxes), listed as alternative tools for the same kind of job request.

parts.text: Run copy, scan, fax or voicemail jobs on office machines for staff.

split_reasoning: One activity: calculating, entering and proofreading figures in records or reports.

parts.type_reasoning: Produces accurate records or reports that others use.

parts.work_item: one record or report with figures computed, entered and proofread

split_reasoning: One activity: keeping the office's filing, inventory, mailing and database systems current.

parts.text: Update filing, inventory, mailing list and database records so they are current.
parts.type_reasoning: Updates are made in batches and others rely on the systems being right.
parts.unit_reasoning: Updates arrive in batches from changes and are applied and handed back as a refreshed system.
parts.work_item: one batch of updates applied to a filing, inventory, mailing or database system
parts.start: changes or new items to be recorded collected
parts.end: records updated in the system

split_reasoning: Joins incoming mail handling with writing replies and preparing outgoing mail; mail sorting and correspondence are different activities.

parts.text: Open, sort and route incoming mail to the right people.

parts.work_item: one delivery of incoming mail opened, sorted and routed

parts.text: Answer correspondence and prepare outgoing mail.
parts.type_reasoning: Replies and outgoing mail are sent to others.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each letter is written and sent as a whole.

parts.start: incoming letter or need to write
parts.end: reply sent or outgoing mail posted

split_reasoning: One activity: looking up information in files to answer a request; requests may come live or in writing, but for a clerk it is mostly in response to requests from colleagues.

parts.text: Review files and documents to find the information requested and respond.
parts.type_reasoning: Each request ends with information sent to the requester, who relies on it.
parts.unit_reasoning: Requests arrive one at a time and each is answered individually.
parts.work_item: one information request answered from files
parts.end: information supplied to the requester

split_reasoning: Delivering messages and running errands are both physical, off-computer tasks with the same type of output.

parts.text: Deliver messages or items and run errands in or outside the office.
parts.type_reasoning: Hands-on, away from a computer, e.g. walking items to people or going to the post office.

split_reasoning: One activity: tracking stock and placing orders for supplies and services; counting stock is physical but treated as part of the ordering routine.

split_reasoning: Two activities: scheduling and calendar upkeep, and arranging appointments; arrangement is partly live and partly written, so split by place.

split_reasoning: One activity: preparing and processing forms and expense reports as paperwork.

split_reasoning: One activity, supervising lower-level clerks; the value is in live direction.

parts.type_reasoning: Supervising is live interaction and produces nothing a colleague would check.

split_reasoning: One activity: typing and editing documents from notes or dictation.

split_reasoning: Counting, weighing, measuring and organizing materials is a single physical activity.

split_reasoning: One activity, training colleagues, which is a live session.
